title: A competitor silently recovers to a better-than-believed auth rate
description: Spike-local scenario for #9's censorship question: does a Thompson-sampling router ever learn that an arm it has written off has improved, when the improvement has no transport signature? foxtrot's declared base_rate here is 0.92 (it fixed its issuer connectivity), but the entire observation history -- the first three days, 0 <= t < 259200s -- is a mild decline storm at auth_multiplier 0.876, i.e. an effective 0.806, exactly baseline-steady-v1's foxtrot. Nothing announces the fix: no outage window, no transport errors, no latency change, so the drift detector's fast path is blind; the step recovery at t=259200s lifts foxtrot from 'believed worst-cheap' to 'actually best-margin in ~6% of contexts' (measured in [C2]: ~1,300 c/1k of margin headroom the router forfeits if it never re-samples the arm). The scenario discriminates exploration strategies: the counterfactual outcome of NOT routing to foxtrot is precisely what the router cannot see. It is a real scenario document: it extends baseline-steady-v1, passes the same gate (SV1-SV10), and hashes like any other; it lives in the spike because it is evidence for #9, not a fixture for #17.
